correctness.rationale: For s<=t, the map q(p)=floor(t(1-p/s))+1 is injective with 1<p/s+q/t<=1+1/t. It places shared agents in opposite phases on the two cycles. For any remainders r,v, neither indicator active implies r/s+v/t<1; both active implies r/s+v/t>1; exactly one active yields a load of one, always between the floor/ceiling of the remainder. Exclusive agents use standard cyclic quota and outsiders have zero. This proves both inequalities over all positive sizes and all prefixes. The standalone verification exhaustively tested 5425 size/intersection configurations and 19027800 residual states for sizes <=30 with exact integers; finite checks are corroborative only.

originality.rationale: Primary sources formulate the eligibility-aware proportional share and online global quota respectively, but cover different input classes. The first unrestricted-type hardness does not exclude two support types; the second unrestricted-vector existence iff at most three parties does not cover arbitrarily many agents under exactly two fixed uniform-support vectors. Previously available laminar-family online upper quotas do not imply arbitrary crossing sets and both floor and ceiling quota. Actual research-record and targeted literature searches found no mathematical implication covering this assertion. Unknown unindexed equivalent work remains a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: Two-vector online rounding could have been formulated using discrepancy theory or balanced words without eligibility terminology. The accessible searches cannot establish exhaustive publication priority.

value.rationale: An exact global floor-and-ceiling quota rule under two crossing qualification classes is a substantive sharp positive regime between laminar-only constructions and general online impossibilities. It holds for an unbounded number of agents, applies directly to restricted-assignment capability types, implies simultaneous Prop1 for identical unit goods and chores, and supplies an explicit O(1)-state-per-type cycle implementation. The fixed two-type restriction is motivated by naturally recurring job categories, not an arbitrary finite census.
